kicker: Prime Agent, read from the source

scenes.headline: How Prime Agent turns every tool into Python
scenes.sub: Prime Intellect's open-source coding agent, and the typed bridge behind its kernel.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Sorbet! Prime Agent gives its model one tool, a Python kernel. Here's what sits behind it.

scenes.text: One tool: a persistent Python kernel. Loops, files and subagents become code the model writes, and the tool schema moves behind the kernel.
scenes.say: The idea: one tool, a persistent Python kernel. Loops, files and subagents become code. The schema doesn't vanish; it moves behind the kernel.

left.title: A tool menu
items: A JSON schema per tool, every request
Each step of a loop is a model turn
left.say: A usual harness re-sends every tool schema with each request, and each step of a loop costs a model turn.

right.title: One Python kernel
items: One parameter: a string of code
A loop over 60 files is one call
right.say: Here, a loop over sixty files is one call, and its results stay in a variable for later.

steps.say: The model writes a string of code. A persistent IPython kernel runs it, and variables, imports and open files survive between turns.
Files, shell and MCP servers are plain Python, run with your permissions. That half really is unbounded.
Agent control is different. Spawning a child or opening a goal crosses to the TypeScript host: twenty-one typed handlers, most on only by flag.
A spawned child returns a handle at once, works in its own session, and reports back by message.

scenes.title: How the harness edits itself
scenes.say: State that outlives a turn goes through one command: refine.

items.say: It reads the trajectory and past refinements.
It proposes small edits: prompt notes, memories, skills, subagent roles.
Host code, not a prompt, rejects any edit to the base system prompt.
Every pass is logged, so a bad edit rolls back to a recorded version.

scenes.text: Prime Agent didn't abolish the tool schema. It demoted it, out of the prompt and into a private typed bridge.

recap: One tool: a persistent Python kernel
21 typed handlers behind it, gated by flag
A harness that edits all but its base prompt
scenes.say: To recap: one kernel, a typed bridge, and a harness that can't rewrite its rules.
